sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Both kérek and szeretnék mean roughly 'I'd like', but szeretnék (from szeret, to like/love) is the more polite, softer conditional form, while kérek is the everyday direct way to ask.

items.spanish: Kérek egy kávét és egy teát.
items.english: I'd like a coffee and a tea.

sections.content: You can mix both in the same conversation — neither is wrong; they're just different registers.
